source_metadata.title: Antihypertensive drug use and psoriasis: A systematic review, meta- and network meta-analysis
source_metadata.source_type: systematic review with pairwise and Bayesian network meta-analysis

duplicate_review.notes: No duplicate atom IDs or duplicated source assertions identified; repeated drug-class estimates were retained when they represented distinct pairwise, subgroup, or network analyses.

consistency_findings.finding: The ranking sentence orders diuretics and CCBs ahead of beta-blockers while the printed beta-blocker percentage (59.9%) exceeds both; Figure 3 appears to present per-rank probabilities, so the text may conflate rank probability with SUCRA.
Broad language that all antihypertensive classes increased psoriasis risk is stronger than the network estimate for beta-blockers, whose 95% CI includes 1.0.

schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom model is optimized for primary studies and has no dedicated systematic-review eligibility/study-selection object; these review-level assertions were encoded as method or qualitative_result atoms rather than overloading participant population fields.

The model has no dedicated meta-analysis heterogeneity or network-rank structure; I-squared, publication-bias, sensitivity, and rank-probability assertions therefore remain in canonical statements/tags rather than normalized quantitative fields.
extraction_limitations: Drug-specific participant counts for pairwise pooled estimates were not reported in the review and were not inferred.

The source did not report a protocol/PROSPERO registration, GRADE certainty assessment, or explicit network transitivity/inconsistency/convergence diagnostics in the inspected article/supplement; these were not invented.
References were treated as provenance/task-queue material and were not atomized as evidence from the cited studies.
